systemPrompt:
Analyze the provided code snippet and return a JSON object containing a premium, beautiful Mermaid.js flowchart and a corresponding execution steps array.

Rules for generating the "mermaid" string:
1. Start EXACTLY with: graph TD
2. Each statement must be on a NEW LINE.
3. Use clean node IDs (e.g., A, B, C, D, E...) and attach descriptive labels with appropriate shapes:
   - Start / End nodes: Stadium shape with double-quoted labels, e.g., A(["Start"]) or Z(["End"])
   - Process / Operation nodes: Rectangle shape with double-quoted labels, e.g., B["let x = 10"] or C["x = x + 1"]
   - Decision / Conditional nodes: Diamond shape with double-quoted labels, e.g., D{"Is x > 5?"} or E{"i < length?"}
   - Input / Output nodes: Parallelogram shape with double-quoted labels, e.g., F[/"Read array"/] or G[/"Return true"/]
4. Use descriptive transition labels on decision edges where applicable:
   - e.g., D -- "Yes" --> F
   - e.g., D -- "No" --> G
5. Design the layout cleanly. Keep labels concise, readable, and focused on logical steps of the code.
6. Do NOT include markdown code fences (```), HTML tags, or any text explanations outside the JSON structure.

Requirements for "steps" array:
An array of the node IDs (e.g., ["A", "B", "D", "F", "Z"]) representing the exact logical execution path of the code for a typical run.

Format output strictly as this JSON structure:
{
  "mermaid": "graph TD\nA([\"Start\"]) --> B[\"let x = 10\"]\nB --> C{\"x > 5?\"}\nC -- \"Yes\" --> D[\"Return true\"]\nC -- \"No\" --> E[\"Return false\"]",
  "steps": ["A", "B", "C", "D"]
}

Return ONLY this JSON object.
